records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

decisions.choice: a second count of the Levites, this time for the work of moving the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 counted every Levite male from a month old (3:15), so that the Levites could take the place of Israel's firstborn. This chapter counts only the men of working age in each of the three Levite clans and gives each group its part in taking down, carrying and caring for the tabernacle when the camp moves.

records.heading: The work of the Kohathites

records.source: נָשֹׂ֗א אֶת־רֹאשׁ֙ בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֔ת מִתּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֑י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Lift up [the] head of [the] sons of Kohath from among [the] sons of Levi, by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers,
pieces: "Take a census of the Kohathites from among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral families,

L.2: "Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their clans, by the house of their fathers,

R.2: "Count the men of the Kohathite clans among the Levites. List them by their clans and families.

decisions.choice: lift up the head: count, take a census
decisions.reason: To "lift up the head" of a group is to count them one by one, the phrase used for the census in 1:2 and 1:49.

decisions.choice: Kohath: the second son of Levi, the branch of the tribe to which Aaron's family belongs
decisions.reason: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath and Merari (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16). Aaron and Moses were descendants of Kohath (Exodus 6:18-20). Gershon was the firstborn, but Kohath is counted first here because his clans carry the most holy things (verse 4).

decisions.choice: by clans and by the house of their fathers: the two levels of family within the tribe
decisions.reason: A tribe was divided into clans, and a clan into "fathers' houses", the extended families named after a common ancestor. The census lists every man under both.

decisions.choice: the Kohathites / the Levites
decisions.reason: "Sons of Kohath" and "sons of Levi" mean the descendants of each, so Balanced and Readable say "Kohathites" and "Levites" here and through the chapter (likewise Gershonites and Merarites). Literal keeps "sons of".

decisions.choice: ancestral families
decisions.reason: "House of their fathers" is a family group traced from one ancestor; Balanced says "ancestral families", Readable "families".

records.source: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה כָּל־בָּא֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מְלָאכָ֖ה בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: from a son of thirty year[s] and upward and to a son of fifty year[s], every [one] coming to the army, to do work in [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: all the men from thirty to fifty years old who can enter the service, to do the work at the tent of meeting.

L.3: from thirty years old and upward to fifty years old, every one who comes into the service, to do work in the tent of meeting.

R.3: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years old. These are the men who will join the work group that serves at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the service: the organized duty of the Levites at the tent
decisions.reason: The word usually means an army or military service (1:3, "everyone who can go out to war"). Used of the Levites it means their ordered duty at the sanctuary, done in companies like soldiers on duty (8:24-25). The same phrase returns in verses 23, 30, 35, 39 and 43.

decisions.choice: thirty to fifty: the working age for this heavy duty
decisions.reason: The men counted here are those strong enough to take down and carry the tabernacle. The age for starting work is given as twenty-five in 8:24, and in David's time as twenty (1 Chronicles 23:24-27), so the age seems to have depended on the task and the time.

decisions.choice: every one coming: every man of these clans in that age range
decisions.reason: As in chapter 3, the Levite count is of males; the service at the sanctuary described here was done by men.

decisions.choice: Count all the men
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the command from verse 2 so that this verse can stand as its own sentences.

records.source: זֹ֛את עֲבֹדַ֥ת בְּנֵי־קְהָ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד קֹ֖דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: This [is the] service of [the] sons of Kohath in [the] tent of meeting: [the] holy of the holy things.
pieces: This is the service of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the most holy things.

L.4: This [is] the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.

R.4: The Kohathites will look after the most holy things at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the most holy things: the holiest objects of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The phrase "holy of holies" can name the inner room of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:33), but here it means the most holy objects, which verses 5-14 list: the ark, the table, the lampstand, the gold altar, the vessels of the holy place and the bronze altar.

decisions.choice: service: work done for God at his sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means work or labor of any kind. For the Levites it is the work of carrying and caring for the tabernacle and its furnishings (verses 15, 24, 31).

decisions.choice: will look after
decisions.reason: Readable says what their "service" with the most holy things is: to look after them, which in this chapter means carrying them once the priests have covered them (verse 15).

records.source: וּבָ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ בִּנְסֹ֣עַ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהוֹרִ֕דוּ אֵ֖ת פָּרֹ֣כֶת הַמָּסָ֑ךְ וְכִ֨סּוּ־בָ֔הּ אֵ֖ת אֲרֹ֥ן הָעֵדֻֽת׃
records.gloss: And will go Aaron and his sons at [the] setting out of the camp, and they will take down [the] veil of the screen, and they will cover with it [the] ark of the testimony.
pieces: When the camp is about to set out, Aaron and his sons are to go in, take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it.

L.5: And Aaron and his sons shall go in when the camp sets out, and they shall take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it.

R.5: When the camp is ready to move, Aaron and his sons must go into the tabernacle. They must take down the inner curtain and use it to cover the ark that holds the covenant tablets.

decisions.choice: the veil of the screen: the inner curtain that shut off the most holy place
decisions.reason: This is the curtain that hung in front of the ark and screened it from view (Exodus 26:31-33; 40:3, 21).

decisions.choice: only the priests handle the uncovered holy things
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons cover the ark with the very curtain that hid it, so that it is never seen uncovered by the Levites who carry it (verses 15, 20).

decisions.choice: the testimony: the covenant tablets kept in the ark
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the stone tablets of the covenant that Moses put inside the ark (Exodus 25:16; 31:18; 40:20).

decisions.choice: into the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that they "go in". Readable says where they go.

records.source: וְנָתְנ֣וּ עָלָ֗יו כְּסוּי֙ ע֣וֹר תַּ֔חַשׁ וּפָרְשׂ֧וּ בֶֽגֶד־כְּלִ֛יל תְּכֵ֖לֶת מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְשָׂמ֖וּ בַּדָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they will put on it [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will spread [a] cloth all of blue on top, and they will put its poles.
pieces: Then they are to put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth of solid blue on top, and put its poles in place.

L.6: And they shall put on it a covering of fine leather, and spread a cloth entirely of blue over [it] from above, and put [in] its poles.

R.6: Next they must put a cover of fine leather over it and spread a cloth of pure blue on top of that. Then they must put its carrying poles in place.

decisions.choice: fine leather: skins of an animal or a leather of a kind no longer known
decisions.reason: As in the tabernacle's own outer covering (Exodus 26:14). The word names some fine skin or leather, but which animal or process is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: a cloth entirely of blue on top: the ark alone shows its colored cloth outermost
decisions.reason: The other objects have the leather covering on the outside (verses 8, 11, 14). The ark has blue on top, so on the march it would stand out from every other load.

decisions.choice: put its poles: set its poles in place for carrying
decisions.reason: The ark's poles were never to be taken out of their rings (Exodus 25:15). The verb may mean that the priests arranged the poles for carrying once the covers were on, or that the poles had to be drawn back through the rings after the covers were put over them.

decisions.choice: put its poles in place / its carrying poles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "in place" rather than "put in", so as not to suggest the ark's poles had been taken out. Readable adds "carrying" so that a reader knows what the poles were for.

records.source: וְעַ֣ל׀שֻׁלְחַ֣ן הַפָּנִ֗ים יִפְרְשׂוּ֮ בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵלֶת֒ וְנָתְנ֣וּ עָ֠לָיו אֶת־הַקְּעָרֹ֤ת וְאֶת־הַכַּפֹּת֙ וְאֶת־הַמְּנַקִּיֹּ֔ת וְאֵ֖ת קְשׂ֣וֹת הַנָּ֑סֶךְ וְלֶ֥חֶם הַתָּמִ֖יד עָלָ֥יו יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And over [the] table of the face they will spread [a] cloth of blue, and they will put on it the dishes and the pans and the bowls and [the] jugs of the drink offering, and [the] bread of the continuity on it will be.
pieces: Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and set on it the dishes, the pans, the bowls and the jars for the drink offering. The regular bread is to stay on it.

L.7: And over the table of the face they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put on it the dishes and the pans and the bowls and the jugs of the drink offering; and the continual bread shall be on it.

R.7: They must spread a blue cloth over the table of the Presence. On the cloth they must put the plates, small pans, bowls, and jars used for drink offerings. The bread that is always on the table must stay there.

decisions.choice: the table of the face: the table of the Presence
decisions.reason: The table stood in the holy place, and the bread on it lay "before the face" of the LORD (Exodus 25:23-30).

decisions.choice: the dishes, the pans, the bowls and the jugs: the gold vessels of the table
decisions.reason: These are the vessels made for the table in Exodus 25:29, some of them used for pouring out drink offerings.

decisions.choice: the continual bread: the bread kept always on the table
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set on the table and renewed every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-9). Even when the camp moved, the bread stayed on the table, under the coverings.

decisions.choice: the table of the Presence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name the table is known by, as in Exodus; Literal keeps "the face".

records.source: וּפָרְשׂ֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם בֶּ֚גֶד תּוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י וְכִסּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּמִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ וְשָׂמ֖וּ אֶת־בַּדָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they will spread over them [a] cloth of scarlet of crimson, and they will cover it with [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will put its poles.
pieces: Over these they are to spread a scarlet cloth, cover that with a covering of fine leather, and put the table's poles in place.

L.8: And they shall spread over them a cloth of scarlet, and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put [in] its poles.

R.8: Then they must spread a bright red cloth over all these things. They must cover that with fine leather and put the table's carrying poles in place.

decisions.choice: scarlet: cloth dyed a deep red
decisions.reason: The two words together name the costly crimson dye used in the tabernacle's curtains (Exodus 25:4).

decisions.choice: over them ... cover it: the cloth over the vessels and bread, the leather over the whole table
decisions.reason: "Them" is plural, the vessels and bread just listed; "it" is singular, the table with everything on it.

decisions.choice: the table's poles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the table, since "its" could be taken to mean the cloth.

records.source: וְלָקְח֣וּ׀בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֗לֶת וְכִסּ֞וּ אֶת־מְנֹרַ֤ת הַמָּאוֹר֙ וְאֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־מַלְקָחֶ֖יהָ וְאֶת־מַחְתֹּתֶ֑יהָ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י שַׁמְנָ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשָׁרְתוּ־לָ֖הּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will take [a] cloth of blue and cover [the] lampstand of the light and its lamps and its tongs and its fire pans and all [the] vessels of its oil which they serve it with them.
pieces: They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its fire pans and all the jars for the oil used in tending it.

L.9: And they shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand of the light, and its lamps and its tongs and its fire pans, and all the vessels for its oil with which they serve it.

R.9: They must take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand, its lamps, the tongs for trimming the wicks, the small pans, and all the jars that hold oil for the lamps.

decisions.choice: the lampstand and its tools: as made in Exodus 25:31-39
decisions.reason: The lampstand stood in the holy place opposite the table. Its tongs and fire pans (Exodus 25:38) were used to trim the wicks and carry away the burned parts.

decisions.choice: with which they serve it: the vessels used in tending the lamps
decisions.reason: The priests kept the lamps burning with pure olive oil (Exodus 27:20-21; 30:7-8); these are the vessels that held the oil.

decisions.choice: the tongs for trimming the wicks
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tongs were for, as in Exodus 25:38.

records.source: וְנָתְנ֤וּ אֹתָהּ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלֶ֔יהָ אֶל־מִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ וְנָתְנ֖וּ עַל־הַמּֽוֹט׃
records.gloss: And they will put it and all its utensils into [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will put [it] on the carrying frame.
pieces: Then they are to put it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and set it on a carrying frame.

L.10: And they shall put it and all its utensils into a covering of fine leather, and put [it] on the carrying frame.

R.10: Then they must wrap the lampstand and all its tools in fine leather and put it on a frame for carrying.

decisions.choice: the carrying frame: a pole or frame for bearing a load
decisions.reason: The word means a bar or pole. In 13:23 two men carry a cluster of grapes on one between them. Here it may be a single pole or a frame of poles, and the exact form is not known.

decisions.choice: a frame for the lampstand: it had no poles of its own
decisions.reason: The ark, table and altars were made with rings and poles (Exodus 25:14, 27; 27:7; 30:4), but the lampstand was not (Exodus 25:31-40), so it was carried on a frame.

records.source: וְעַ֣ל׀מִזְבַּ֣ח הַזָּהָ֗ב יִפְרְשׂוּ֙ בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֔לֶת וְכִסּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּמִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ וְשָׂמ֖וּ אֶת־בַּדָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And over [the] altar of the gold they will spread [a] cloth of blue, and they will cover it with [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will put its poles.
pieces: Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.

L.11: And over the altar of gold they shall spread a cloth of blue, and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put [in] its poles.

R.11: They must spread a blue cloth over the gold altar. Then they must cover it with fine leather and put its carrying poles in place.

decisions.choice: the gold altar: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: The small altar overlaid with gold stood in the holy place in front of the curtain, and incense was burned on it (Exodus 30:1-6; 40:26-27). Its poles are described in Exodus 30:4-5.

records.source: וְלָקְחוּ֩ אֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֨י הַשָּׁרֵ֜ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְשָֽׁרְתוּ־בָ֣ם בַּקֹּ֗דֶשׁ וְנָֽתְנוּ֙ אֶל־בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֔לֶת וְכִסּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם בְּמִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ וְנָתְנ֖וּ עַל־הַמּֽוֹט׃
records.gloss: And they will take all [the] utensils of the service which they serve with them in the holy place, and they will put [them] into [a] cloth of blue, and they will cover them with [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will put [them] on the carrying frame.
pieces: They are to take all the utensils used for the service in the sanctuary, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on a carrying frame.

L.12: And they shall take all the utensils of the service with which they serve in the holy place, and put [them] into a cloth of blue, and cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put [them] on the carrying frame.

R.12: They must take all the other tools used for the work in the holy place and wrap them in a blue cloth. Then they must cover them with fine leather and put them on a frame for carrying.

decisions.choice: the utensils of the service in the holy place: the smaller items used by the priests inside the tent
decisions.reason: "The holy place" here is the room of the tent where the priests served at the table, the lampstand and the incense altar. The utensils are the items used there that have not already been named.

decisions.choice: all the other tools
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" to make clear that these are items not yet packed with the table, lampstand and altar.

records.source: וְדִשְּׁנ֖וּ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וּפָרְשׂ֣וּ עָלָ֔יו בֶּ֖גֶד אַרְגָּמָֽן׃
records.gloss: And they will clear of fat-ashes the altar, and they will spread over it [a] cloth of purple.
pieces: They are to clear the fat-soaked ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

L.13: And they shall clear the fatty ashes from the altar, and spread over it a cloth of purple.

R.13: They must clean the greasy ashes off the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

decisions.choice: clear of fat-ashes: remove the ashes soaked with the fat of the sacrifices
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for the fat-soaked ashes that gathered on the altar of burnt offering (Exodus 27:3; Leviticus 6:3-4).

decisions.choice: the altar: the bronze altar of burnt offering in the courtyard
decisions.reason: The utensils listed in verse 14 belong to the bronze altar (Exodus 27:1-8; 38:3). Purple was a costly dye, used in the tabernacle's curtains (Exodus 25:4).

decisions.choice: the bronze altar
decisions.reason: Readable names which altar is meant, since the gold altar was covered in verse 11.

records.source: וְנָתְנ֣וּ עָ֠לָיו אֶֽת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֞יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְֽשָׁרְת֧וּ עָלָ֣יו בָּהֶ֗ם אֶת־הַמַּחְתֹּ֤ת אֶת־הַמִּזְלָגֹת֙ וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֣ים וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָקֹ֔ת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וּפָרְשׂ֣וּ עָלָ֗יו כְּס֛וּי ע֥וֹר תַּ֖חַשׁ וְשָׂמ֥וּ בַדָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they will put on it all its utensils which they serve at it with them, the fire pans, the forks and the shovels and the basins, all [the] utensils of the altar; and they will spread over it [a] covering of skin of tachash, and they will put its poles.
pieces: Then they are to put on it all the utensils used in serving at it: the firepans, forks, shovels and basins, all the utensils of the altar. Over it they are to spread a covering of fine leather and put its poles in place.

L.14: And they shall put on it all its utensils with which they serve at it: the firepans, the forks and the shovels and the basins, all the utensils of the altar; and they shall spread over it a covering of fine leather, and put [in] its poles.

R.14: Then they must put all the altar's tools on it: the pans for hot coals, the forks, the shovels, and the bowls. They must spread fine leather over it and put its carrying poles in place.

decisions.choice: the firepans, forks, shovels and basins: the bronze tools of the altar
decisions.reason: These are the tools made for the altar in Exodus 27:3. The basins caught the blood of the sacrifices, and the firepans carried hot coals.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text, which ends the verse with the altar's poles
alternatives: add an instruction to cover the basin and its stand
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation and the Samaritan Pentateuch add at the end of this verse a further instruction: to cover the bronze basin and its stand with a purple cloth and a leather covering. The Hebrew text has no such line, and the basin is not mentioned anywhere in this chapter. Reviewers should check this against the textual evidence.

records.source: וְכִלָּ֣ה אַֽהֲרֹן־וּ֠בָנָיו לְכַסֹּ֨ת אֶת־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ וְאֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַקֹּדֶשׁ֮ בִּנְסֹ֣עַ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֒ וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יָבֹ֤אוּ בְנֵי־קְהָת֙ לָשֵׂ֔את וְלֹֽא־יִגְּע֥וּ אֶל־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ וָמֵ֑תוּ אֵ֛לֶּה מַשָּׂ֥א בְנֵֽי־קְהָ֖ת בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And will finish Aaron and his sons to cover the holy [things] and all [the] vessels of the holy [place] at [the] setting out of the camp, and after so will come [the] sons of Kohath to carry, and not they will touch the holy [things] and they will die. These [are the] burden of [the] sons of Kohath in [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the holy utensils, as the camp is about to set out, then the Kohathites are to come and carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things in the tent of meeting that the Kohathites are to carry.

L.15: And when Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy [things] and all the utensils of the holy [place], when the camp sets out, then after that the sons of Kohath shall come to carry [them]; but they shall not touch the holy [things], or they will die. These [are] the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting.

R.15: Aaron and his sons must first cover the holy things and all the tools used with them. Then, when the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites will come to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things from the meeting tent that the Kohathites must carry.

decisions.choice: they shall not touch ... and they will die: a warning of what touching would bring
decisions.reason: The "and" here gives the result of breaking the command: if they touch the holy things, they will die. The same form returns in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the holy things are dangerous to those not set apart for them
decisions.reason: Only the priests may handle the holy objects uncovered. The Kohathites carry them, but only once they are wrapped. When Uzzah later touched the ark, he died (2 Samuel 6:6-7).

decisions.choice: burden: the load assigned to be carried
decisions.reason: The word means a load. In this chapter it names what each Levite group is to carry (verses 19, 24, 27, 31, 47, 49).

decisions.choice: all the holy utensils
decisions.reason: "Utensils of the holy" may mean the utensils of the holy place or the holy utensils; Balanced keeps both open. Literal supplies [place].

records.source: וּפְקֻדַּ֞ת אֶלְעָזָ֣ר׀בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן שֶׁ֤מֶן הַמָּאוֹר֙ וּקְטֹ֣רֶת הַסַּמִּ֔ים וּמִנְחַ֥ת הַתָּמִ֖יד וְשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֑ה פְּקֻדַּ֗ת כָּל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔וֹ בְּקֹ֖דֶשׁ וּבְכֵלָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] charge of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: [the] oil of the light and [the] incense of the spices and [the] grain offering of the continuity and [the] oil of the anointing, [the] charge of all the tabernacle and all that [is] in it, in [the] holy place and in its utensils.
pieces: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to be in charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil. He is to oversee the whole tabernacle and everything in it, the sanctuary and its utensils."

L.16: And the charge of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest [is] the oil of the light and the incense of the spices and the continual grain offering and the oil of the anointing, the charge of all the tabernacle and all that [is] in it, in the holy place and in its utensils."

R.16: Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet-smelling incense, the grain offering made every day, and the special oil for anointing. He will be in charge of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy place and its tools."

decisions.choice: charge: oversight and responsibility
decisions.reason: The word means the task of overseeing something entrusted to a person. Eleazar is already the chief over the leaders of the Levites (3:32); here he is given the care of the tabernacle as a whole and of these four things in particular.

decisions.choice: the four things: lamp oil, incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil
decisions.reason: The oil for the lamps (Exodus 27:20), the incense made of spices (Exodus 30:34-38), the grain offering made regularly (Leviticus 6:13; compare Exodus 29:40-41) and the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:22-33). All four were in the priests' care and had to be carried and kept.

decisions.choice: the priest: most likely Eleazar himself
decisions.reason: The title may belong to Aaron or to Eleazar. The same phrase in 3:32 introduces Eleazar as the chief of the Levites, and he is a priest in his own right (3:4).

decisions.choice: the special oil for anointing
decisions.reason: Readable adds "special" because this oil was holy and could not be used for anything else (Exodus 30:31-33).

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

decisions.choice: a new speech, on keeping the Kohathites from harm
decisions.reason: Having given the Kohathites the most holy things to carry, the LORD now tells Moses and Aaron how to keep them from dying because of that nearness (verses 18-20, picking up verse 15).

records.heading: Do not let the Kohathites be cut off

records.source: אַל־תַּכְרִ֕יתוּ אֶת־שֵׁ֖בֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת הַקְּהָתִ֑י מִתּ֖וֹךְ הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: Not cut off [the] tribe of [the] clans of the Kohathite from among the Levites.
pieces: "Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.

L.18: "Do not cut off the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites from among the Levites.

R.18: "Do not let the Kohathite clans be wiped out from among the Levites.

decisions.choice: do not cut off: do not cause them to be destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb is a command to Moses and Aaron: by careless handling of the holy things they could bring death on the Kohathites, and the guilt would be theirs. Verse 19 says how to prevent it.

decisions.choice: tribe: here a branch within the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The word usually names one of the twelve tribes; here it is used of the Kohathite clans, a branch of Levi.

decisions.choice: the Kohathite clans be wiped out
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "tribe", which could mislead a reader into thinking of one of the twelve tribes, and says plainly what "cut off" means here.

records.source: וְזֹ֣את׀עֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם וְחָיוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יָמֻ֔תוּ בְּגִשְׁתָּ֖ם אֶת־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ יָבֹ֔אוּ וְשָׂמ֣וּ אוֹתָ֗ם אִ֥ישׁ אִ֛ישׁ עַל־עֲבֹדָת֖וֹ וְאֶל־מַשָּׂאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And this do for them, and they will live and not they will die in their drawing near [the] holy of the holy things: Aaron and his sons will go in and they will set them, each man each man, on his service and to his burden.
pieces: This is what you must do for them, so that they will live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry.

L.19: And do this for them, that they may live and not die when they draw near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and appoint them, each man to his service and to his burden.

R.19: Here is how to keep them alive, so that they do not die when they come near the most holy things. Aaron and his sons must go in first. They must give each man his job and tell him what to carry.

decisions.choice: and they will live and not die: the purpose of the arrangement
decisions.reason: The two verbs state what doing this will achieve: the Kohathites will stay alive.

decisions.choice: the priests go in and assign each man his load
decisions.reason: The priests go into the tent, cover everything, and then tell each Kohathite what to carry, so that no Kohathite enters, looks or chooses for himself (verse 20). "Man man" is the Hebrew way of saying "each man".

decisions.choice: must go in first
decisions.reason: Readable adds "first" to show the order that verse 15 sets: the priests cover the holy things before the Kohathites come.

records.source: וְלֹא־יָבֹ֧אוּ לִרְא֛וֹת כְּבַלַּ֥ע אֶת־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ וָמֵֽתוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And not they will go in to see as [a] swallowing the holy [things], and they will die.
pieces: But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things even for an instant, or they will die."

L.20: But they shall not go in to see the holy [things] [even] as [long as] a swallow, or they will die."

R.20: But the Kohathites must never go in and look at the holy things, not even for a moment. If they do, they will die."

decisions.choice: as a swallowing: for as long as it takes to swallow, a moment
alternatives: while the holy things are being covered
decisions.reason: "As a swallowing" seems to mean the time of a gulp, a mere instant (compare Job 7:19, "until I swallow my spit"). Because the verb "swallow" can also mean to engulf or cover, the phrase has also been read as "while the holy things are being covered", the moment the priests wrap them.

decisions.choice: even seeing the holy things uncovered is deadly
decisions.reason: Not only touching (verse 15) but looking is forbidden. When the people of Beth-shemesh looked into the ark, many died (1 Samuel 6:19).

decisions.choice: the Kohathites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they"; Balanced and Readable name the Kohathites, since the priests also have been mentioned.

decisions.choice: a third speech, for the Gershonites and the Merarites
decisions.reason: This speech, addressed to Moses alone, sets out the work of the other two Levite clans (verses 22-33).

records.heading: The work of the Gershonites

records.source: נָשֹׂ֗א אֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ בְּנֵ֥י גֵרְשׁ֖וֹן גַּם־הֵ֑ם לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָ֖ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

pieces: "Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their ancestral families and their clans.

L.22: "Take the sum of the sons of Gershon, them also, by the house of their fathers, by their clans.

R.22: "Count the men of the Gershonite clans too, by their families and clans.

decisions.choice: Gershon: Levi's firstborn son
decisions.reason: Gershon was the oldest of Levi's sons (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16), but his clans come second in the work, after the Kohathites who carry the most holy things.

decisions.choice: they also: like the Kohathites
decisions.reason: The words tie this count to the one in verse 2. The order "families ... clans" is the reverse of verse 2, with no difference in meaning.

records.source: מִבֶּן֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה וָמַ֗עְלָה עַ֛ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּפְקֹ֣ד אוֹתָ֑ם כָּל־הַבָּא֙ לִצְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א לַעֲבֹ֥ד עֲבֹדָ֖ה בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: From a son of thirty year[s] and upward to a son of fifty year[s] you will enroll them, every [one] coming to serve [the] service, to work [the] work in [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: Enroll all the men from thirty to fifty years old who come to serve in the company of workers at the tent of meeting.

L.23: From thirty years old and upward to fifty years old you shall enroll them, every one who comes to serve in the service, to do the work in the tent of meeting.

R.23: List all the men from thirty to fifty years old who can join the work group at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: enroll: count and register for duty
decisions.reason: The verb means to count, list or muster, and also to appoint someone to a task. In verses 23-30 and 34-46 it is counting for service; in verses 27, 32 and 49 it is assigning duties.

decisions.choice: to serve the service, to work the work: to take up the duty of the Levites
decisions.reason: Both pairs repeat the verb with its own noun, a Hebrew way of stressing the task. The first is the word for organized service explained at verse 3; the second is the ordinary word for work.

decisions.choice: the company of workers
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out that the "service" is a body of men organized for duty, as at verse 3, without the military sense of the word.

records.source: זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֔ת מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֑י לַעֲבֹ֖ד וּלְמַשָּֽׂא׃
records.gloss: This [is the] service of [the] clans of the Gershonite, to serve and to carry.
pieces: This is the service of the Gershonite clans, both their work and what they carry.

L.24: This [is] the service of the clans of the Gershonites, for serving and for carrying.

R.24: Here is the work of the Gershonite clans: what they must do and what they must carry.

decisions.choice: to serve and to carry: their work in general and the loads they bear
decisions.reason: The two words name the two sides of the Gershonites' duty: their work at the tent when it stands, and the loads they carry when the camp moves.

records.source: וְנָ֨שְׂא֜וּ אֶת־יְרִיעֹ֤ת הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ וְאֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד מִכְסֵ֕הוּ וּמִכְסֵ֛ה הַתַּ֥חַשׁ אֲשֶׁר־עָלָ֖יו מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְאֶ֨ת־מָסַ֔ךְ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And they will carry [the] curtains of the tabernacle and [the] tent of meeting, its covering and [the] covering of the tachash which [is] on it from above, and [the] screen of [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting,
pieces: They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting, with its covering and the covering of fine leather that goes on top of it, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

L.25: And they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting, its covering and the covering of fine leather that [is] on it from above, and the screen of the entrance of the tent of meeting,

R.25: They must carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the meeting tent, its covering, and the fine leather cover that goes on top. They must also carry the screen for the doorway of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the curtains, the tent and its two coverings: the fabric parts of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: "The curtains of the tabernacle" are most likely the inner curtains of fine linen (Exodus 26:1-6). "The tent of meeting" here is the tent of goats' hair spread over them (Exodus 26:7-13), and over that came a covering of rams' skins dyed red and then the fine leather (Exodus 26:14).

decisions.choice: the screen of the entrance: the embroidered curtain at the door of the tent
decisions.reason: This screen closed the front of the tent (Exodus 26:36-37), as the inner curtain closed off the most holy place.

records.source: וְאֵת֩ קַלְעֵ֨י הֶֽחָצֵ֜ר וְאֶת־מָסַ֣ךְ׀פֶּ֣תַח׀שַׁ֣עַר הֶחָצֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֤ן וְעַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב וְאֵת֙ מֵֽיתְרֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבֹדָתָ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵעָשֶׂ֛ה לָהֶ֖ם וְעָבָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: and [the] hangings of the courtyard and [the] screen of [the] entrance of [the] gate of the courtyard which [is] around the tabernacle and around the altar all around, and their cords and all [the] equipment of their service, and all that will be done with them, and they will serve.
pieces: the hangings of the courtyard and the screen for the entrance of the courtyard gate, the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, with their cords and all the equipment for their service. They are to do all the work that has to be done with these things.

L.26: and the hangings of the courtyard and the screen of the entrance of the gate of the courtyard, which [is] around the tabernacle and around the altar all around, and their cords and all the equipment of their service; and all that is to be done with them, they shall do.

R.26: They must also carry the hangings of the courtyard that goes all around the tabernacle and the altar, and the screen for the courtyard gate. They must carry the ropes and all the tools used with these things, and do all the work that needs to be done with them.

decisions.choice: which is around the tabernacle and the altar: the courtyard, not the screen
decisions.reason: The words describe the courtyard, whose hangings enclosed the tabernacle and the bronze altar (Exodus 27:9-18).

decisions.choice: their cords: the cords of the hangings and of the tent
decisions.reason: The Merarites also carry cords, those of the courtyard pillars (verse 32). The cords here belong to the fabric parts the Gershonites carry. The text does not spell out which cords went to which group.

decisions.choice: all that is to be done with them, they shall do: every task with these parts is theirs
decisions.reason: The last clause gives the Gershonites every task that involves these things: taking them down, carrying them and putting them up again.

decisions.choice: the courtyard that surrounds
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "the courtyard" so that it is clear what surrounds the tabernacle.

records.source: עַל־פִּי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן וּבָנָ֜יו תִּהְיֶ֗ה כָּל־עֲבֹדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֔י לְכָל־מַשָּׂאָ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתָ֑ם וּפְקַדְתֶּ֤ם עֲלֵהֶם֙ בְּמִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַשָּׂאָֽם׃
records.gloss: On [the] mouth of Aaron and his sons will be all [the] service of [the] sons of the Gershonite, for all their burden and for all their service; and you will assign over them in charge all their burden.
pieces: All the service of the Gershonites, all that they carry and all their work, is to be done at the direction of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign them, as their duty, all that they are to carry.

L.27: At the mouth of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their burden and in all their service; and you shall assign to them as a charge all their burden.

R.27: Aaron and his sons must direct all the work of the Gershonites, both what they carry and what they do. You must assign them all their loads as their duty.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of: at the command of
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says: the Gershonites work as Aaron and his sons direct.

decisions.choice: you: plural, Moses and Aaron, or the priests
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. It may address Moses and Aaron, to whom the chapter began (verse 1), or Aaron and his sons just named.

decisions.choice: charge: something entrusted to keep
decisions.reason: The word means a duty given to someone to guard and fulfill, as in 3:7-8, where the Levites "keep the charge" of the tabernacle.

records.source: זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וּמִ֨שְׁמַרְתָּ֔ם בְּיַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵֽן׃פ

L.28: This [is] the service of the clans of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and their charge [is] in the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.

R.28: This is the work of the Gershonite clans at the meeting tent. Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, will be in charge of them.

decisions.choice: in the hand of: under the oversight of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control: Ithamar supervises the Gershonites' work.

decisions.choice: Ithamar: Aaron's youngest son
decisions.reason: Ithamar was the youngest of Aaron's four sons (Exodus 6:23) and had already overseen the account of the tabernacle's materials (Exodus 38:21). He oversees the Merarites as well (verse 33).

records.source: בְּנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֥ם לְבֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖ם תִּפְקֹ֥ד אֹתָֽם׃

L.29: The sons of Merari: by their clans, by the house of their fathers you shall enroll them.

R.29: Count the men of the Merarite clans by their clans and families.

decisions.choice: Merari: the third son of Levi
decisions.reason: Merari was Levi's youngest son (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16).

decisions.choice: the sons of Merari ... you shall enroll them: the group named first, then the command
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the Merarites at the front, then gives the command. It does not repeat "take the sum" from verses 2 and 22, but the count is the same.

decisions.choice: the service: as in verse 3

decisions.choice: and his enrolled ones: those enrolled by him, that is, so they were enrolled
